newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UN reports new burst of violence in Burundi.
newsitem.headline: UN reports new burst of violence in Burundi.

text.p: The U.N. said on Friday that tens of people were dying daily in new outbreaks of violence in southern Burundi, where a mainly Tutsi army is warring majority Hutu rebels.
U.N. spokeswoman Therese Gastaut said the latest violence in the southern regions of Bururi and Makamba had displaced large numbers of civilians but she gave no details.

The army, which grabbed power in a coup last year, announced this week that it had killed at least 300 Hutu rebels in Bururi since April 5 for the loss of six soldiers after it said a force of up to 3,000 rebels attacked from bases in Tanzania.
In another incident, Gastaut said suspected rebels killed 38 highschool students and seven teachers in an attack on a school at Buta, near Bururi town, on April 30.
Another 40 students were wounded in the attack, she said, quoting reports from Burundi-based U.N. human rights observers.

The violence in southern Burundi is relatively new. The fighting has spread to most of the countryside in the past year, making travel outside the ethnically cleansed capital Bujumbura extremely dangerous.
More than 150,000 people, mostly civilians, have been killed in massacres and civil war in Burundi since Tutsi troops killed Burundi's first Hutu president in 1993.
Burundian Hutu rebels of the National Council for the Defence of Democracy were uprooted from their bases in Zaire last year when Zairean Tutsi-dominated rebels seized the area.
